text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam, Ms Joan Pereira and Miss Cheryl Chan raised suggestions on healthcare affordability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We share the sentiment of Members that peace of mind is important.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Helping our elderly with their healthcare costs is a joint responsibility with the Government through subsidies, collective risk pooling in our community through insurance, and individual and family support through MediSave and personal savings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This is a hallmark of a caring and inclusive society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We have enhanced the reach of Government subsidies over the years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Through CHAS, we have made outpatient care in the community more affordable, including for the management of chronic diseases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: To Ms Rahayu Mahzam's query, we continue to review the CHAS criteria.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: And, as with all schemes, there could be people who fall outside the eligibility criteria.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: But we are open to consider such cases on appeal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: With the PG Package, all Pioneers enjoy special CHAS support above the CHAS blue tier, and an additional 50% off subsidised treatments at polyclinics and public specialist outpatient clinics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We have also made it easier to utilise MediSave for healthcare needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The number of conditions covered under the Chronic Disease Management Programme (CDMP) has been progressively expanded over the years, and Singaporeans can now use MediSave to pay for 19 conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Singaporeans aged 65 and above can also utilise an additional $200 of their MediSave through the Flexi-MediSave Scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will continue to review our healthcare financing schemes to ensure affordability for Singaporeans while also ensuring sustainability of our healthcare system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We made MediShield Life a universal health insurance scheme in 2015.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: To ensure affordability, premium subsidies are extended to the lower- and middle-income.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This has been a relief for many older Singaporeans and a valuable assurance that their large hospital bills are covered by insurance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: ElderShield is also currently being reviewed to provide stronger support for disability in old age.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We welcome the recommendations and will work with the Committee to consider how best to target support for those who may need more help with their premiums.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: There have been some questions on why the Committee recommended lowering the inclusion age to 30.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The Committee explained that lowering the inclusion age for ElderShield distributes an individual's own premium payment over a longer period during his working years to pay for his own future needs when he grows old.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The premiums paid are for their own long-term care needs and are not intended for the young to subsidise the elderly for their long-term care needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In fact, the very intent of tapping on insurance is to avoid shifting the financial burden to the young.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: I also note Ms Joan Pereira's suggestion to review our nomenclature for ElderShield.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We would like to assure everyone that no Singaporean will be denied appropriate healthcare.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For those who continue to have difficulties with their healthcare bills, additional support is available through MediFund.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Third, at the community level, we want to build stronger communities of care to complement families in supporting our seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This is especially important as family size shrinks and increasingly more elderly will live by themselves.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: An area of focus for MOH is to work with both community-based voluntary welfare organisations (VWOs) and our healthcare providers to integrate health and social support for our seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For instance, AIC has worked with VWOs to station care teams within senior activity centres to do regular checks and support the activities of daily living of seniors living alone in rental precincts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We agree with Dr Lily Neo that technology can present new opportunities to bolster our community support for seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For instance, in the SHINE Seniors project at Marine Parade, sensors are placed in the homes of seniors living alone, so that VWO staff or volunteers can respond to calls for help.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Another example is Changi General Hospital's Care Line, which is a 24-7 call centre that can respond to calls for help from seniors living alone in the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We are also conducting a nationwide pilot of tele-rehabilitation that allows seniors to follow up with their rehabilitation exercises in the comfort of their homes, post discharge from hospitals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Khoo Teck Puat Hospital is also using telehealth consultations to support new nursing homes in better managing residents who are near the end of life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Given the magnitude of population ageing, formal services alone are not enough.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: I agree with Mr Henry Kwek, Ms Tin Pei Ling, Miss Cheng Li Hui and Ms Rahayu Mahzam that we need to rally the whole community to come together to support our seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We would like to thank our Members who have spoken out in support of these initiatives and helped with bringing our communities together on the ground.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The CNS initiative was introduced in Budget 2016 as a pilot of what would eventually serve as a national community-based support system to help our seniors age well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In essence, it coordinates a strong local network of health and social care partners to support seniors, as a complement to family support, enabling our seniors to age confidently in the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For well seniors, we want to keep them active and healthy for as long as possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For those who are lonely, we find them a friend.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: And for those with multiple needs, our aim is to get them holistic help quickly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: CNS has been piloted in Tampines, Choa Chu Kang and Marine Parade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: As Members have heard from Miss Cheng Li Hui, it has been well-received by all stakeholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Based on what we have learnt from CNS, we plan to strengthen this effort.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: More details will be announced at the Committee of Supply this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: However, our success in building communities of care hinges on support and partnership from the wider community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Therefore, I fully support Mr Kok Heng Leun's suggestion to step up public education and promote greater awareness of the process of ageing and the needs of seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will continue to invest in public education.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Longevity is a blessing and not to be spent in sickness or loneliness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: If we can work together, ageing need not be feared.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We can enable seniors to age positively with purpose and grace, empower strong families that can care for seniors, and build a cohesive and resilient community able to thrive in the face of population ageing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: MOH and the Ministerial Committee on Ageing look forward to working with all Members and Singaporeans to realise a "Nation for All Ages".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: (In Mandarin):   After hearing Mr Kok Heng Leun's speech, I was very touched.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Illness and death are inevitable, but it is important that we enable our seniors to age positively with purpose, gracefully and with dignity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The Government will continue to work hard to build a Nation for All Ages that is caring and inclusive and embrace seniors as an integral part of our community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: But family and kinship are priceless and irreplaceable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We should honour the elderly as we do our own aged parents.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: The Ministry of Manpower, together with our tripartite partners, is committed to supporting our older workers to enjoy fulfilling years and engage in productive work.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We expect this trend to continue in the foreseeable future as Singaporeans live longer and healthier.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: It is a good thing that our seniors can work and want to work longer.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Active participation in the workforce allows seniors to make positive contributions and forms part of active ageing.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: The economy and society as a whole benefit from their expertise and experience.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: To this end, we should continue to support older workers to have meaningful employment opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: At the same time, we should also ensure that our older workers are treated fairly and with respect at our workplaces.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Our tripartite partners have been working closely together to help support our older workers so that they can have longer and fuller working lives.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: This applies to the public and private sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Of those who accepted re-employment in the same job at age 62, around 96% did not receive any cut in their basic salaries in 2012.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: And this proportion rose to 98% in 2016.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Some Members have suggested why not remove the retirement age and re-employment age altogether?

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: First, the retirement age of 62 provides older workers peace of mind that employers are not allowed to terminate their employment simply based on age.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Second, with the re-employment age, the older workers are further protected as employers must offer eligible workers re-employment up to age 67.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Third, the introduction and progressive raising of re-employment age, instead of retirement age, balances the employers' need for business flexibility and the employment needs of the older workers better.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: While the employer is obliged to offer re-employment to the older worker at 62 till 67, it need not necessarily be for the same job or at the same pay.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: There is some flexibility so long as both employers and employees achieve a mutual agreement.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: And also, beyond the re-employment age, older workers can continue to work as long as there is mutual consent between them and the employers.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: With extended lifespans and improved health among seniors, there will be scope to raise the age of re-employment further again over time.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: This, however, will be a matter for tripartite deliberations.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: For now, as the re-employment age was just raised from 65 to 67 last year, the immediate focus of the Government and the tripartite partners is to ensure successful implementation of the new re-employment age to benefit more older workers.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: This is to fulfil what we had set out earlier.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: As we encourage employers to hire and retain older workers, we recognise that those who do so deserve extra support and encouragement.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: An additional wage offset of up to 3% of monthly wages is also provided to encourage continued employment of older workers above the re-employment age of 67.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We also support employers to provide flexible work arrangements (FWAs) for older workers who prefer to transit from full-time employment to take on more flexible work options.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Our various programmes to improve the employability and employment of older workers have shown encouraging results.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Singapore's employment rate of residents aged 65 to 69 is 41.5% in 2016.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: This compares quite favourably with developed economies, with Singapore ranked 5th against 35 Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) countries in 2016.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: It is also higher than some of the developed countries with no retirement age, such the US at 31%, Australia at 25.9%, the UK at 21% and Denmark at 19.1%.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: For older workers to work productively and also to help companies to remain competitive, we must ensure that our workplaces are age-friendly.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We must treat our older workers fairly with dignity.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: MOM and our tripartite partners are against age discrimination.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: The Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP) promotes the employment of older workers and raises awareness of the value that older workers bring to the workplace.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: They look into all age discrimination complaints and refer cases to MOM for investigation where warranted.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Enforcement actions will be taken against employers who discriminate based on age.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: The Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices (TGFEP) also spells out the principles of fair and merit-based employment which we expect all employers to abide by.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: For example, job applicants should be assessed fairly and are not to be ignored or rejected on the basis of age.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: This applies to all jobs listed in the JobsBank.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: The Guidelines also state specifically that date of birth information should not be asked in the job application forms.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: This is an encouraging start, but we should do more.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: I urge more employers to tap on WorkPro to take bold steps to redesign and create meaningful jobs for older workers.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Third, we need both our older workers and employers to play their parts to enhance the employment and employability of mature workers.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We will keep strengthening our support to them through SkillsFuture and Adapt and Grow.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: I encourage more employers and workers to take full advantage of these Government schemes we have put in place for them.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: With an ageing workforce and the fast pace of economic restructuring and transformation, we will need to do even more to ensure that our future workforce will remain inclusive.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office and for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Together with our tripartite partners, we will press on in our efforts to support our seniors so that they can continue to lead an active and fulfilling life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI) agrees with the concerns raised by Mr Henry Kwek, Ms Tin Pei Ling, Ms Joan Pereira and other Members.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This workgroup has representatives from the public, private and people sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Later in the year, we will be explaining in more detail our strategies to help all Singaporeans, especially the most vulnerable, to understand and enjoy the benefits of technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In the interim, we have agreed on some broad principles that will inform these strategies and plans that we develop.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Third, the greatest reach and impact in this space will be achieved only through the deep collaborations between the people, public and private sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: First, we have over 30 senior-friendly infocomm learning hubs island-wide, including at community centres (CCs) and libraries that offer a customised curriculum to train seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These are known as Silver Infocomm Junctions (SIJs).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Second, the "Seniors for Smart Nation" series of courses, run by the "Senior Academy" programme of PA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Third, the "IM Bonding" programme at Senior Activity Centres focuses on lower-income elderly and involves a significant aspect of social interaction.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Fourth and last, the Silver Infocomm Wellness Ambassador is a programme to train and support seniors to teach and encourage their peers about technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Although there has been a lot of work ongoing for the last 10 years, much remains to be done.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are all ageing, technology will continue to develop at a rapid pace, and making sure the elderly benefit from the progress of our society must be something we always pay attention to.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I begin with thoughtful planning and design of our infrastructure.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling, Miss Cheryl Chan, Ms Joan Pereira and Dr Lily Neo spoke about how we should design and retrofit our Housing and Development Board (HDB) flats, estates and public infrastructure to enable our seniors to age actively, comfortably and safely.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Today, when building our new estates, HDB’s consultants adopt the Building and Construction Authority's (BCA’s) Accessibility Code and guidelines.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, common spaces are designed with ramps instead of just steps and seamless barrier-free routes to connect various amenities for our seniors and those who are wheelchair-bound.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Three-generational fitness and play facilities facilitate social interaction between our seniors and the community.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Within our flats, senior-friendly features are provided, such as gentle gradients at the main entrance, common bathrooms that are wheelchair-accessible and more user-friendly clothes drying systems.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The bigger challenge has been to retrofit our older, mature estates to make them more senior-friendly.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And we have been doing this assiduously over many years since the 2000s, adding more ramps, linkways and senior-friendly facilities to mature estates through programmes, such as the Neighbourhood Renewal Programme (NRP) and Community Improvement Projects Committee (CIPC).

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Making our mature estates elderly-friendly requires a community effort.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: That is why programmes, such as NRP and CIPC, are structured to allow the community to participate in decision-making.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Private building owners can also tap on BCA's Accessibility Fund.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This provides co-funding to encourage them to retrofit their private buildings that pre-date 1990, to make them senior-friendly.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I next turn to housing asset monetisation, a point raised by various Members.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh, Ms Rahayu Mahzam, Ms Chia Yong Yong and Mr Henry Kwek suggested ways to help seniors unlock more value from their homes to supplement their retirement needs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Currently, LBS is not open to households in larger flats as they have more monetisation options than those in smaller flats.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For instance, they can right-size to a smaller flat in the same neighbourhood.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Under the Seniors Priority Scheme, seniors, including those in private properties, enjoy priority when they apply for a 2-room flexi flat in the same town or estate as their current home.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: If seniors living in larger flats right-size to a 2- or 3-room flat, they may apply for the Silver Housing Bonus and receive a cash bonus, if they use some of their proceeds to top up their CPF Retirement Accounts and join CPF LIFE.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To raise awareness of these and other monetisation options, HDB works with our media, organises public talks and seminars and sets up booths at local community events.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Seniors also receive personalised information on their monetisation options when they carry out housing transactions at our HDB counters.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Most recently, HDB and CPF Board sent out individually customised mailers to seniors about the range of monetisation options that are available to them.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Henry Kwek, Ms Chia Yong Yong and Mr Gan Thiam Poh suggested other ways of monetising properties which do not require our seniors to move home, such as reverse mortgages and specialised funds based on the French concept of "Viager".

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Financial institutions (FIs) are already allowed to offer reverse mortgages and these specialised funds.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But both are complex financial products which are more difficult to understand, hence the challenge.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The risk that the value of the payouts may exceed that of the property could also impact their attractiveness to home owners.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Recent surveys also found that many seniors were generally averse to the idea of reverse mortgages as they preferred to remain debt-free at that stage in life.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Some of the options I mentioned earlier, like buying a 2-room flexi flat with priority allocation, are also open to seniors living in private properties who may wish to consider asset monetisation.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In addition, with the changes announced by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) in March 2017, they may also obtain mortgage equity withdrawal loans from FIs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: MAS had announced that such loans that are less than 50% of the market value of the property would no longer be subject to the Total Debt Servicing Ratio (TDSR) framework.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This may help retirees, many of whom would have paid up most of their outstanding housing loan, monetise part of the value of their property if they wish.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To do so, we have to plan well ahead.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This involves nurturing communities of care, strengthening community care and service delivery for vulnerable seniors, planning ahead for seniors who may lose or have lost mental capacity, and putting in place laws to protect vulnerable seniors.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The composition of families has shifted over the years.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Family sizes are shrinking, and we see more seniors who live alone or without children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Because of this changing profile, we have to proactively ramp up efforts to complement family support while, at the same time, encourage the strengthening of family ties.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Henry Kwek and Ms Joan Pereira suggested introducing Senior Care leave to employees caring for their parents.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Caregivers of elderly parents need support and understanding, and I thank Mr Kok Heng Leun for his very heartfelt and personal sharing of his experience, for the benefit of this House.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We encourage employers to provide a family-friendly workplace, and have introduced several family leave enhancements over the last few years.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In the meantime, we will continue to work with the tripartite partners to encourage employers to adopt family-friendly practices, including adopting the Tripartite Standard of FWAs, and better leveraging on the Worklife Grant.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To foster community interaction, we now build 2-room flexi flats in the same block as larger flat types for most projects.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Under the Multi-Generation Priority Scheme, married children and their parents are given priority if they apply for a pair of flats at the same level, block or Build-To-Order (BTO) project.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Those who wish to live as a multigenerational family can apply for 3Gen flats.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Henry Kwek made some thoughtful recommendations on retirement housing, while Mr Leon Pereira spoke about assisted living for seniors.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We also agree with Dr Lily Neo that we should support our seniors to live independently in their homes and communities for as long as possible.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Our strategy to achieve this is to try to integrate the delivery of social and care services within our public housing estates, for ease and convenience of our seniors.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Over the years, we have ramped up the introduction of eldercare facilities in our HDB estates.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have taken this one step further with Kampung Admiralty, where seniors living in and around the Kampung can obtain a continuum of social and health services at the Active Ageing Hub.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh will also be glad to know that we will continue working with MOH to explore new senior-friendly housing models, such as new forms of home and care options to allow seniors to age in a familiar environment and to remain independent for as long as possible.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This includes assisted living developments that will help to expand the care and residential options available to seniors, by integrating senior-friendly housing and senior care services.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is currently under study and we will announce more details when ready.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: At the same time, we are studying measures which can better facilitate the development of private housing projects to support the needs of our seniors.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are reviewing our Development Control guidelines to provide more clarity on retirement housing developments, and we will share more information on these plans when ready.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam spoke about the need to support vulnerable seniors in our midst.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This means empowering them to make choices to remain healthy, active and socially connected in their golden years, enabled collectively by the family, community and state.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: On community support, we have expanded our network of social services supporting the low-income and vulnerable seniors, in close partnership with VWOs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Through the SCNs, we have supported these low-income and vulnerable seniors to stay engaged in the community, prevent social isolation and receive timely and coordinated care.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Frail seniors with social and health needs are case-managed by social workers in the Cluster Support teams who coordinate care together with AIC.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Senior Group Homes (SGHs) can support frail seniors who are suitable for communal living.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: SSOs play the important role of coordinating complex cases, which often involve multiple agencies and organisations.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: SSOs also plan and coordinate services at the local level and manage MSF-funded regional services for families and seniors.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: While social service delivery has improved over the years, we know that we can continue to do better.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Today, a family with multiple needs has to navigate different schemes, programmes, agencies and VWOs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We want to improve our interagency work processes to provide more integrated and holistic support for those in need.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: One of our key enablers will be CNS, which is being piloted, to bring together healthcare and social agencies and the community to provide support for seniors.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We can also improve data sharing and use among Government agencies and with the community.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This could reduce the need for clients to submit the same documents to different agencies and organisations multiple times.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It also helps to harness the time, energy and skills of social service professionals and volunteers to better support our seniors.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan suggested improving the outreach and awareness of the Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA), by making certifiers of LPAs more easily accessible within the community.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Many of them are GPs who operate in clinics in the heartlands.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In addition, there are community services that provide regular legal clinics for both LPA as well as will-writing.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: An example is Life Point, started by Sheng Hong Welfare Services.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It is a popular one-stop service for seniors to make their LPAs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We welcome more organisations to start similar services to benefit our seniors.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: If a person loses mental capacity without having made an LPA, their family members or friends may apply to the Court to be appointed as their deputy.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To support our ageing seniors who lack family support and experience declining mental capacity, we are also piloting a new initiative known as the Community Kin Service or Comm Kin Service.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Under this service, VWOs can apply for a Court order to manage the senior’s money in order to meet the senior’s day-to-day needs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: What they need to do is to prepare a care plan detailing the kinds of expenses that need to be incurred for their daily needs for these seniors and present them to Court.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Once approved, they will act within the remit of the Court order.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It thus empowers VWOs to do more to support seniors holistically within the community.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Nonetheless, we still encourage Singaporeans to make an LPA because an LPA offers them choice and autonomy in deciding who they wish to appoint as their proxy decision-maker, and gives peace of mind to the family, knowing that the necessary preplanning has been done.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam and Ms Chia Yong Yong had asked us to review the role of the Tribunal of Maintenance of Parents (TMP).

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Maintenance of Parents Act (MPA) provides legal recourse for seniors 60 and above and who are unable to provide for themselves to claim maintenance from their children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We recognise that some parents may be unwilling to file an application against their own children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, the Act, therefore, allows the Commissioner to resolve issues through conciliation, without the need for the commencement of legal proceedings at TMP.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: If the parent is unable to make an application himself, for example, due to physical infirmity, the Commissioner is able to apply on behalf of the parent, with his consent.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Thus far, the Commissioner has not had to make such an application to the Tribunal on behalf of a parent, as most family members step up to help the parent.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will, however, continue to actively look into ways to lower the barriers for a senior to apply for maintenance, even as we seek to strengthen familial ties.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Ms Chia Yong Yong also asked whether the Tribunal has ever ordered children, under section 6 of MPA, to maintain their parents by setting up a trust fund to pay out regular maintenance.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Thus far, the Tribunal has not made such orders.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Most orders have been by way of cash payment or cash support.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Currently, going beyond adjudication and mediation, TMP may already refer a parent to SSO for financial assistance and advice, if he is not awarded any maintenance, or if the maintenance awarded is insufficient to meet basic needs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The parent and the children may also be referred to an FSC for case management and counselling.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: That, in a way, also addresses the point Ms Rahayu Mahzam brought up.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: She suggested that the Tribunal take on more family counselling and mediation roles.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Many suggestions have been given, including looking into the law of presumption of advancement.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: All these are things that we will study in the course of our work.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Concurrently, it is imperative that we put in place safeguards to ensure that frail elderly and ageing persons with disabilities are able to live in an environment that is free from abuse, neglect and self-neglect.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Before I close, allow me to make this very quick observation.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are encouraged that all Members who have spoken have given good ideas, given heartfelt examples of cases and individuals whom they have encountered.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: At the end of the day, this has to be a whole-of-Singapore effort, involving families and communities, to make Singapore an inclusive and caring home that embraces all our seniors.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: We have worked hard and deserve to be tired.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: But fatigue aside, hearing the insights from my colleagues here remind me why Parliament inspires.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: The scale and scope of these ideas today can only be described as breathtaking.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Mr Leon Perera described it as an inescapable part of the human condition.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Therefore, the Members of this House believe that dealing with ageing starts with ourselves.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Miss Cheryl Chan called for seniors to cultivate the "undefeated mind", one filled with hope, will and imagination.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Miss Cheryl Chan and Dr Lily Neo pointed out that we are personally responsible for our own health.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Otherwise, we will not enjoy our long life.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Ms Chia Yong Yong cautioned us to be wise in estate planning.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Better for our seniors to make wills and, therefore, have more control over their fates.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Many of my colleagues here believe that after the individual, the next line of responsibility lies clearly with the families.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: But as Ms Chia Yong Yong said, while the Government can work harder to ensure that families step up, we must "do not and must not abrogate the basic human values of filial piety." After all, one cannot legislate filial piety.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: We must all be filial, however, because, as Dr Intan Mokhtar mentioned, "it is the right thing to do".

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Ms Chia Yong Yong also shared that we have obligations even if there is no love.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: And as Mr Kok Heng Leun shared, being a dutiful caregiver to our parents is not just a responsibility, but it can also be one we derive joy from.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Helping our ailing parents is an intimate process.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: It promises the possibilities of transforming and deepening our precious relationships with those closest to us.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Therefore, Mr Gan Thiam Poh, Dr Intan Mokhtar and Ms Rahayu Mahzam calls for all of us – Government, society, community – to do what is necessary to promote the right values of filial piety.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Just this year, at my constituency, we started teaching filial piety through Confucian Dizi Gui.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: And I look forward to encouraging similar classes through other cultural lenses.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Today, we also talked about more support for caregivers.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Ms Joan Pereira, Mr Kok Heng Leun and myself spoke about caregiver leave, so that our seniors will not be facing the trauma of sickness and hospital visits alone.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: This will also provide some comfort to caregivers.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Mr Kok Heng Leun also suggested more tax relief for caregivers, and Miss Cheryl Chan suggested more generous subsidies for caregiver services.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Next, we must also ensure that seniors are on the right side of the digital divide.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling mentioned that we should strive to ensure that both "hardware and heartware are elderly-friendly" and we should not just be talking about technology but also processes.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Ms Joan Pereira, Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Ms Tin Pei Ling also asked us to tap on the full possibilities of digital eldercare and call for the Government to limit the downside of embracing everything digital to our parents.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: We also spoke about senior housing and monetisation of assets.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Dr Lily Neo, Ms Tin Pei Ling and Mr Leon Perera spoke about encouraging and teaching good designs, building housing close to necessities.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Ms Cheryl Chan suggested auditing all towns for such.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: I also spoke about more options for private developers in assisted living and nursing home, as well as catalysing more reverse mortgages for private estates.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: On the financial side, our speakers have acknowledged that the Government has done much.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: But there is always a little bit more room to do more, especially if we can continue to grow our economy and keep our medical costs low.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: The first line of financial support is actually for our seniors to stay employed and self-reliant.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: In terms of senior employability, both Dr Lily Neo and Dr Intan Mokhtar asked that we relook at employment and re-employment ages.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling asked the Government to take the lead in senior employment and spearhead new designs and job designs and work environment.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Mr Leon Perera spoke about using technology and innovation to expand on employability of seniors.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: I concur on his points and I spoke previously on using the shared economy to create micro-jobs for our seniors.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Ms Joan Pereira, Dr Lily Neo and Miss Cheryl Chan asked for more support for community healthcare programmes with more emphasis on disease prevention.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling, Dr Lily Neo and Mr Leon Perera also asked the Government to accelerate our local pace of digital eldercare innovation.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh called for more increases in home care medical services, and Ms Joan  Pereira asked for more dementia friendly communities as well as getting the review of ElderShield right.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Beyond finance and health, Members also believe about emotional well-being.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: We believe that our seniors, even if they retire, should stay active.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: As Ms Tin Pei Ling hopes, "we can continue to contribute because we want to.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: It brings meaning to life, it helps us look forward to every new day.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Is it not wonderful?" As such, Ms Joan Pereira proposed the innovative idea of encouraging time-banking, which is not just to encourage seniors to volunteer, but also to spur bartering of services among seniors.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Dr Lily Neo also suggested a one-stop for volunteer advisory.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: But sometimes, our seniors also need community support, especially on the emotional front.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Getting Government support for coordination through CNS will give our community efforts a major push.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Members of this House also spoke about fighting misperceptions.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling asked us to "stamp out ageism".

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: In fact, I think we must go beyond stemming out ageism.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Dr Lily Neo and Mr Leon Perera asked all of us to focus on bringing out the best of our seniors, focus on the Silver Dividends, rather than worry about the demographic time bomb.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: We are a decisive country, and we think long term.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: If we come together as a society, we can get on the right side of ageing.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: The stakes are high for us because all Singaporeans, every member of this Chamber, own this challenge together.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: We will all be that statistic, that group that would tap on Government funds, that would add to the healthcare cost, that would need to be cared for." But beyond Government programmes, we must also step as a society by creating and participating in community initiatives.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: And specifically for Members in this Chamber, we have an added responsibility as the local leaders capable of pulling together hearts, minds, and hands, in our own respective areas.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: And so, we, in this Chamber, must all step up.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: As Ms Pei Ling puts it, "a caring and inclusive society cannot be one when citizens only talk about and expect somebody else to do it.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: We all have a duty to do it".

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: And when we discharge our duties to our families and seniors, we, like Mr Kok Heng Leun, who cared for his father, can see the world through his eyes, and discover empathy in ourselves and in our society.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: I would also like to thank the Government for providing such a comprehensive response across five Ministries.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: I am glad to hear from Minister of State Sam Tan about our Government's progressive take towards retirement and re-employment.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: I take his point that the private sector needs time to get used to the recent changes.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: At the same time, I would like to remind our seniors that their fate is largely in their own hands.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: There is no legal limit on when we can stop working, as long as there is demand for us.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: If seniors can ensure that their skillsets stay relevant, they will be prized for both their skills and wisdom over time.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary and Senior Minister of State Amy Khor have shared excellent examples of how we can apply technologies to help our seniors.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: More flexibility there can do wonders to provide much needed housing options, especially for our seniors living in private estates.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Having said that, it is clear that the Ministry of National Development has done much to create new models of housing, especially for the public estates.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: I take MSF's point that companies need time to adjust and adapt before we can pursue further moves.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Until then, I appeal for more companies to apply FWAs to their employees who are caregivers.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: When a company treats employees with compassion, the employees usually respond with passion.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: I hope that the private sector and the social sector can think hard about meeting this need.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: I am also heartened by Senior Minister of State Amy Khor's point about confident ageing, and her progress update on the Action Plan for Successful Ageing.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: In many of the areas raised by my fellow MPs, MOH is either already piloting or is scaling up their existing programme.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: I would also like to thank Minister Gan Kim Yong and Senior Minister of State Amy Khor for the Action Plan for Successful Ageing.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: It is a remarkable plan, the result of painstaking consultation involving more than 4,000 people.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: I hope the ideas discussed today will help strengthen our plan.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Some say that Singapore is too forward oriented from Day 1.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Our founding Prime Minister was all of 36 when he steered a big ship called Singapore.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Since Day 1, we forced the future onto ourselves, in every dimension we can think of.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: When we were still a developing country, international experts said we could not afford the MRT system.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Often, our Pioneers made sacrifices to afford these projects.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Just like their personal sacrifices for their children, this is our seniors' way of saying to us, "we care for you, and we do the best for you”.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Now that we have comfortably crossed our first 50 years, we have passed a milestone.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Singapore must continue to be future-oriented and continue to carry the torch that our founding fathers have passed on to them.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Like the seniors before us, we owe it to our children a duty to build a bright future, sparkling with possibilities.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Only then, when we have done all these, can we say to our caring seniors, who built Singapore, "Do not worry.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Excellent speech, Mr Kwek, but a slight technicality.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: In future, please refer to your Parliamentary colleagues in a slightly formal way than calling them by their first names.
